source_refs.note: 3. Enzyme Concentration: a main subheading of 5.4 Factors affecting the rate of enzyme action, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 135-136.

blocks.text: Enzymes are very efficient and a small number of enzyme molecules can catalyse reactions of large amount of substrate. The overall rate of enzyme-controlled reactions depends directly on the amount of enzyme present at a specific time (if substrate concentration is unlimited). When enzyme concentration increases, there are more enzyme molecules and more active sites. So, more substrate molecules bind with new active sites and are transformed into products. If enzyme concentration goes on increasing but substrate concentration remains the same, no more substrate molecules will attach with enzymes. So, the rate of reaction stays constant and does not increase further (Fig.5.7).

blocks.alt: A graph of rate of reaction against enzyme concentration. The line rises straight from the origin, then bends and runs flat along a dotted level; an arrow at the bend is labelled No more substrate to attach with enzyme.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.7: Effect of enzyme concentration on enzyme activity (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.7).
